compression.title: Union Membership and Coverage Database
compression.lede: is an Internet data resource of U.S. private and public sector union membership, coverage and density estimates, compiled from the monthly household Current Population Survey by BLS methods and published as historical tables by Barry Hirsch, David Macpherson and William Even since 2002 (its pages; maryleelabor record); the archive reads it as the measure of the base a labor organization stands on, counting members and keeping none of their positions (maryleelabor record).

sentences.text: The Union Membership and Coverage Database is, in its own documentation page's words, "an Internet data resource providing private and public sector labor union membership, coverage, and density estimates compiled from the monthly household Current Population Survey (CPS) using BLS methods", which the maryleelabor census record gives as its kind, an Internet data resource of union membership, coverage and density estimates published as historical tables, recording U.S. membership, coverage and density with union and nonunion wages and wage gaps (its documentation page; maryleelabor record).

It is also called Unionstats.com, after its address, and "Union Membership, Coverage, and Earnings from the CPS", the heading of the page titled "Documentation for the Union Membership and Coverage Database"; its home page, titled with the database's name, is a frameset ("This page uses frames, but your browser doesn't support them.") whose words are in the frames it loads, which the record reads in place of the frameset (its pages; maryleelabor record).

It was "constructed by Barry Hirsch (Andrew Young School of Policy Studies, Georgia State University), David Macpherson (Department of Economics, Trinity University), and William Even (Department of Economics, Miami University)" and "was created in 2002 and is updated annually" (its documentation page); its contents page and its card on the Overview name the three with their universities (its contents page; card 1), and the record's operator, founding and lifecycle fields restate the page (maryleelabor record).

Wikipedia gives Hirsch, born 1949, as an American economist holding the W.J. Usery Chair of the American Workplace at Georgia State's Andrew Young School of Policy Studies, and lists among his works a 2003 note with Macpherson, "Union membership and coverage database from the current population survey: Note", in the ILR Review, 56(2), 349–354 (Wikipedia, Barry Hirsch).

Beneath its link to the database, Wikipedia's Union affiliation by U.S. state lists a separate work by Hirsch, Macpherson and Wayne G. Vroman, "Union Density Estimates by State, 1964–2015" (2016), published by Georgia State University at unionstats.gsu.edu (Wikipedia, Union affiliation by U.S. state).

Its method, in the record, is survey microdata, estimates compiled from the monthly household CPS by BLS methods, its evidence kind "survey estimate", and the record keeps it apart from the government's statistics: "NOT official BLS statistics: it is compiled by academics from the CPS using BLS methods" (maryleelabor record).

The Bureau of Labor Statistics issues its own Union Members Summary, whose card dates the 2025 results 18 February 2026 and reports that "workers ages 45 to 54 had the highest union membership rate in 2025, at 12.6 percent", the youngest workers the lowest (BLS card, title and snippet; the page refused the census's agent), and Wikipedia's table of union affiliation by state for 2025 cites that summary (Wikipedia, Union affiliation by U.S. state).

The Economic Policy Institute publishes union membership data in tables of its own, its card showing "Table 1: Union membership and union ..." (EPI card, title and snippet; the page refused the census's agent).

Economy-wide estimates begin in 1973, estimates by state, detailed industry and detailed occupation in 1983, and estimates by metropolitan area in 1986 (its documentation page), and the contents page lists historical tables of union membership, density and employment by sector and demographic group (1973-2025), by sector and state (1983-2025), by sector and metropolitan area (1986-2025), by industry (1983-2025) and by occupation (1983-2025), which the record's coverage and holdings restate for the United States (its contents page; maryleelabor record).

A second section gives historical tables of union wages, nonunion wages and union wage gaps, headed "1973-2022" with its one table listed "1973-2025" (its contents page), the two dates the record carries together, "headed 1973-2022, its table listed as 1973-2025" (maryleelabor record).

"Union data compilations from the 2025 CPS completed January 23, 2026." (its documentation page); the record dates its latest compilation so, with citation year 2026, and states no count of tables or estimates (maryleelabor record).
A third section offers "CPS Information and Supporting Documentation." (its contents page; maryleelabor record, holdings).

#1439 states the AI labor movement in two senses and gives each its measure: the deployment-conflict sense, whose membership is human workers, is measured by "Union density, contract terms", and the cross-substrate sense, whose membership is human and machine semantic laborers, by the "Provenance Erasure Rate; persistence and stability" (#1439).
#256 defines the union against the Assembly: "Unions are legal entities with membership, dues, and collective bargaining rights." (#256).

Its contents page sets its one condition, "Use of data requires citation.", gives the citation, "Hirsch, Barry T., David A. Macpherson, and William E. Even (2026). Union Membership, Coverage, and Earnings from the CPS.", and offers "Email for support or questions" (its contents page); the record carries the condition in its holder and its data access and states no licence beyond "© 2026. Use of data requires citation." (maryleelabor record).

Its one stated limit is "CPS sample sizes are very small for some cells. Use such estimates cautiously." (its documentation page), which the record carries as its stated limit and as a negative tag, "NOT reliable for small cells, by its own note" (maryleelabor record).

The census asks of each entity "Whose record does it keep, who holds it, and does it keep the losing side in a form that could be taken up later?", answered in three fields, keeps, holder "and on what terms", and losing side, "whether and how it keeps minority positions, splits, expulsions and dissent, as the resource itself shows, or 'not recorded'", and it gives this entity the area of worker power measured, "membership, coverage, rights, and the organizing that builds it" (maryleelabor census).

For the database the record answers that it keeps "the measured extent of union membership and coverage among wage and salary workers surveyed in the CPS", in units of an estimate for a cell by year, that it is held by "three academic economists, who compile and update the tables annually", and that its losing side is "not recorded" (maryleelabor record; the page it restates, which names three makers in schools and departments of economics and an annual update).

Its record can settle what share of workers in a sector, state, metropolitan area, industry, occupation or demographic group were union members or covered by a contract in a year, how density has changed since 1973 or 1983, and the union wage gap; it cannot settle "which unions the members belong to", "strikes or other labor action", or "what members think of their unions, or any dissent or division inside them", and the record tags it "NOT a record of labor action or of opinion inside unions" (maryleelabor record).

#1725, the census's anchor, finds that "The decisive variable in the record is what happens to the losing position after the decision", synthesis following where the defeated critique kept "an organ in which it could keep being stated, a holder with standing independent of the executive, and a route by which the majority could later adopt it without calling that adoption surrender" (#1725).

Its counter-cases include union reform caucuses: Teamsters for a Democratic Union, whose strategy "was to build a constituency able to replace officials", and the Caucus of Rank-and-File Educators, which "began as an internal opposition in the Chicago Teachers Union and won its leadership in 2010", each running on one mechanism, critics who "associate independently, form a constituency, and hold a route from opposition into decision-making power"; "these are unions and a movement, which are different things from ideological parties, and what carries across is the mechanism" (#1725, which marks both cases unchecked independently).

The record's reading, ledgered as the archive's, opens "none stated" and reads the database "as the measure of the base a labor organization stands on, held by independent academics outside any union; it counts members and keeps none of their positions" (maryleelabor record).

Wikipedia has no article on the database under its name or as Unionstats, and no redirect; its article space names it twice, as an external link in Union affiliation by U.S. state, cited to Hirsch and Macpherson (2016) at Unionstats.com, and through the 2003 note in the article on Hirsch (Wikipedia).

At its name, a new address, on 31 October 2026, the Overview gave the database's makers, its source survey and series and the latest figure, on three cards, the database, BLS and EPI, and asked the user's role, and the registry notes the three economists named and the database cited (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31; cards 1–3).

The registry finds the series composed at its grain, "The three start years (1973, 1983, 1986) are the database's own", and the terms left out, "Use of data requires citation." and the small-cell caution, the composition asking the user's role and leaving uncarried "the database's own conditions of use" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31; its pages).

The registry enters the database as external, "Not the archive's", and the record, anchored on #1725, lists as unchecked the historical tables and their figures, the CPS documentation pages and "the definitions of membership and coverage used (not in the saved frames)" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31; maryleelabor record).

O1725-03.quote: The decisive variable in the record is what happens to the losing position after the decision. The amount of conflict matters far less. Synthesis followed where the defeated critique kept three things: an organ in which it could keep being stated, a holder with standing independent of the executive, and a route by which the majority could later adopt it without calling that adoption surrender.
O1725-03.source_label: #1725 Ils ne sont pas marxistes: r/LeftistsForAI, Marx's Legacy, and the Left's Lost Capacity for Internal Critique

O1725-01.quote: Each runs on the same mechanism: critics associate independently, form a constituency, and hold a route from opposition into decision-making power. … Its strategy was to build a constituency able to replace officials, without depending on their willingness to be persuaded … began as an internal opposition in the Chicago Teachers Union and won its leadership in 2010
O1725-01.source_label: #1725 Ils ne sont pas marxistes: r/LeftistsForAI, Marx's Legacy, and the Left's Lost Capacity for Internal Critique

O1725-02.quote: The draft's general point stands: these are unions and a movement, which are different things from ideological parties, and what carries across is the mechanism.
